name: pear
why: Peer-to-peer runtime built on Hypercore, a distributed-systems door worth a look even if it is more platform than curiosity.

brief.what_it_is: Pear is an installable peer-to-peer application runtime, plus development and deployment tooling, from Holepunch. You install the pear CLI, then build, share, and run desktop, terminal, or mobile apps that talk directly to other peers without servers. Its own description is 'Build, share, and extend unstoppable, zero-infrastructure P2P apps for mobile, desktop, and terminal.' Apps are developed and released through the CLI (pear stage, pear build, pear touch, pear --menu), and peers receive updates over the air. It runs on Bare, a separate zero-core JavaScript runtime that can also be used on its own. The README's own framing is that the page is a docs landing page, so this entry is drawn from the docs rather than a source repository.
brief.why_it_exists: The docs frame it as a way to build the 'Internet of Peers' with apps that need no server infrastructure. The stated goal is apps that are 'unstoppable' and 'zero-infrastructure', with applications loaded remotely from peers and shared by anyone.
brief.how_it_works: Pear loads applications from peers rather than from a central host, and its desktop architecture combines Electron, Bare worker processes, storage, and over-the-air updates. Networking is built from P2P modules named in the docs: HyperDHT for dialing peers by key, Hyperswarm for topic discovery, Hypercore, Hyperbee, Hyperdrive for storage and replication, and Autobase for shared rooms. The getting-started tutorial describes a chat app whose peers discover each other through the DHT and stream messages directly.

brief.install_notes: Follow the PATH instructions the installer prints, then run pear. The npm-global install is an alternative, described on Install & upgrade. The tutorial expects Node.js v22.17 or newer and npm v10.9 or newer, a POSIX-style terminal (macOS, Linux, or Windows with WSL), and an editor. The pear CLI is only needed for the shipping and updating parts of the tutorial. Templates are cloned from GitHub (holepunchto/hello-pear-electron, plus hello-pear-bare and hello-pear-react-native). Release and multisig steps involve a stage, provision, and multisig flow, which the docs describe as a separate pipeline.
brief.standout: Apps are distributed peer to peer and updated over the air, and the release process includes multisig signing with a 'pear://' upgrade link. Bare is also usable on its own as an embeddable JavaScript runtime, which sets it apart from a plain desktop framework.
brief.status: Appears actively maintained. The docs were recently updated, and they reference Pear 3.2.0 and a current getting-started path, plus a Tether-published Docker image. The fetched pages show no release date or commit history, so exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: Windows support goes through the irm installer or WSL for the tutorial. The tutorial assumes Node 22.17 or newer. Shipping requires the pear CLI and a multisig release flow, which adds setup weight. The docs describe Pear as a platform, not a lightweight tool, so expect a learning curve. I did not find licensing details in the pages I read. Some related pages were not fetched, including the Bare runtime and the release pipeline reference.
quotes: Pear loads applications remotely from peers and lets anyone create and share applications with peers.
Build, share, and extend unstoppable, zero-infrastructure P2P apps for mobile, desktop, and terminal.
Welcome to the Internet of Peers.
